_meta.name: capability registry data
_meta.why: The provider knowledge lives here, not in cap.py. Adding a provider, retiring one, or changing a price/category/credential name is an edit to THIS FILE ONLY. cap.py reads it and never hard-codes a provider.
_meta.owner: the seat that owns scripts/cap/ and docs/capability-registry.md
_meta.never: No credential VALUE may ever be written into this file or any file under scripts/cap/. Only env var NAMES.

credential_sources.label: personal-secretary-mvp/.env (the one env file that holds the provider keys)

search_roots.label: this repo (harness-config)
search_roots.why: the brief's 'some code in this repo'. scripts/deployed/ inside it is a tracked mirror of /home/zabz/bin. Only role=primary roots decide the WIRED flag.
search_roots.prune_reason: journal/ and _scratch/ are prose, not wiring: a name mentioned in a lesson is not a call site. scripts/cap is pruned because it is this registry itself: counting the registry's own provider table as evidence that a provider is wired would be circular.

search_roots.label: /home/zabz/bin (authority node deployments)
search_roots.why: the brief's second path. It is a Linux path on the authority node; on a Windows laptop seat it does not exist and the registry must say so rather than silently skip it. scripts/deployed/ is its tracked mirror.

search_roots.label: personal-secretary-mvp (the application)
search_roots.why: the problem statement says some keys are used by the application. An application reference is reported as provenance but does NOT set WIRED, which the brief defines as this repo or /home/zabz/bin. That is the difference between 'the app uses it' and 'the harness or the fleet is wired to it'.
search_roots.prune_reason: vendored libraries, generated test artefacts, caches and runtime state are not our wiring.

search_roots.label: ~/.dsh harness config (read-only)
search_roots.why: the harness wires model providers here (llm-* apiKeyEnv, agent presets, profiles). Reported as provenance for the same reason as the app. Read only; cap.py never writes under ~/.dsh.
search_roots.prune_reason: session transcripts and caches mention everything and wire nothing.

scan.skip_basenames_reason: a key NAME defined in a credential file is not a use of the provider; only code and config wiring count.

seat.name: mesh child on zabz-yoga (this session)
seat.profile: headless (as reported by the brief: 'a mesh child writes to whichever machine the broker picked')
seat.how_observed: the agent's own tool plane, listed in its runtime context for this session. It is NOT machine-readable from a subprocess, so it is recorded here by hand, with the date, and must be re-observed when the profile changes.
seat.reobserve_with: re-read the seat's tool list and replace observed_tools / observed_mcp_tools here; no code change is needed.
seat.mcp_note: no mcp__* tool is present in this seat's plane. The zabz preset mounts mcp-firecrawl, mcp-jina, mcp-playwright, mcp-secretary (presets/zabz/agent.cordis.yml), but a preset is only loaded by a profile that carries it, and this seat does not. That difference is exactly what the REACHABLE flag is for.
